title: Hidden message in the solved K1-K3 (+ Morse) text: acrostics (1st/2nd/3rd/last letter of words), every k-th word or letter (k up to 40, every start), K2 coordinate digits as step counts, carved-row first/last letters and columns, sentence initials, doubled letters; forwards and backwards; scored against word-order-shuffled texts
k4_result: No K4 involved. K1-K3 (+ Morse) text: 44,876 readings (22,438 rules x 2 directions) of 12+ letters over 24 text styles, 7 scores each, grouped in 3 families (letters from words / letters of the running text / carved rows) = 21 maxima. Combined statistic (-log10 of the smallest Gumbel tail over the 21 maxima): text 1.45, exactly the controls' median (1.44); 732 of 1,500 test controls at least as high, p = 0.49. Per channel nothing stands out after paying for 21 channels: best are rows:wordrun 10 (carved-row column 1 backwards HLHIETRDEFLETEACHOKDCSTOE; controls median 7, max 13; p = 0.053) and letter:qwin -4.07 (every 20th letter backwards ...NOTAREDTEMONTHANTAIEWA...; controls median -4.30, max -3.77; p = 0.055). Acrostic family: longest common-word run 9 letters (controls median 10, max 18; p = 0.99), best 20-letter quadgram window -4.66 (p = 0.69), longest dictionary word 6 (p = 1.0), method words 2 (p = 0.97). Longest dictionary word in any reading: 8 letters (Morse text, every 3rd letter backwards); controls median 8. Short items read by eye: misspelt letters Q U A E U (correct L O E I ON), raised Y A R, word after each X T D W T C, letter before each X D N E E T: nothing.
controls: Same text with the word order shuffled inside each section (K1, K2, K3, Morse separately; keeps every word and letter count): 500 reference controls (for z-scores) + 1,500 test controls (null distribution of every maximum). Controls' combined statistic median 1.44, max 3.63 (K1-K3 1.45).
planted: 3/3 ranked first; 2/3 beat all 1,000 test controls (p = 1/1001 < 0.001), the third p = 2/1001 = 0.002. Planted texts of K1-K3 length with words replaced so that (1) initials of 20 consecutive K2 words spell SHIFTEACHROWBYTHEKEY: combined 4.25 vs controls max 3.66; (2) initials of every 3rd K3 word spell ADDTHECLOCKTIMETOROW: 4.00 vs 3.60; (3) second letters of 20 consecutive K2 words spell READLAYERTWOEASTWARD: 4.24 vs 4.30 (one control in 1,000 beat it through the method-word count of its second-letter line). In all three the top reading held the full message and its common-word run was 20 against controls' max 18-19.
scope_limits: A statistic only. Detects a hidden message of about 20+ letters made of common English words (2,000 most frequent of data/english/words_big.txt plus method/compass words) or reading clearly as English on the big quadgram model; a shorter message, one in rare words, numbers spelt as digits, or a deliberately non-English key word string would not stand out among 44,876 readings (chance gives common-word runs of 13-21 letters in letter-skip readings, 8-19 in acrostic readings). Plain quadgram scores alone cannot find a 20-letter plant at this many readings (0/3 in tuning). Not tested: meaning carried by whole words or by the layout on the copper beyond rows/columns of the carved cipher panel; the tableau panel; the K1-K3 ciphertexts; readings that skip by a varying count other than the K2 coordinate digits/numbers; letter-level k = 1 (the text itself); readings under 12 letters (only printed for a human read); K2 coordinate step counts with a phase other than 0 from starts beyond one cycle (they are suffixes). Q kept/dropped is tied to X kept/dropped. Styles are carved vs corrected spelling, X kept vs dropped, ID BY ROWS vs X LAYER TWO.

negative.family: Hidden message in K1-K3 plaintext (acrostic / skip readings)
negative.hypothesis: Sanborn's 'instructions in the earlier text' are a message spelt by letters picked from the solved K1-K3 text (word initials or n-th letters, every k-th word or letter, coordinate-digit steps, carved-row edges or columns), readable without K4.
negative.scope: K1, K2, K3, Morse and K1-K3 joined in 24 styles (carved/corrected spelling, X and Q kept/dropped, ID BY ROWS / X LAYER TWO); 1st/2nd/3rd/last letter of each word and the letter string; every k-th item k = 1..40 (letters 2..40) from every start; K2 digits 3 8 5 7 6 5 7 7 8 4 4 and numbers 38 57 6 5 77 8 44 as repeating steps from every start in one cycle; first/last letter and each column of the plaintext under the 25 carved cipher rows; sentence initials/finals; doubled letters and the letter after; forwards and backwards; 44,876 readings of 12+ letters; scores: big-model quadgram mean and best 20-letter window, word coverage, longest dictionary word, method-word count, longest run of common words.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: no reading beats word-order-shuffled versions of the same text; combined statistic 1.45 against controls median 1.44, p = 0.49 (732 of 1,500 controls at least as high); best acrostic common-word run 9 letters (controls median 10, max 18) (controls: 500 reference + 1,500 test word-shuffled texts; planted 20-letter instructions in word initials at skip 1 and 3 and in second letters ranked first 3/3, beat all 1,000 controls 2/3, third p = 0.002).

follow_ups: The same battery on the K1-K3 CIPHERTEXT and the tableau panel as carved (rows, columns, every k-th letter), where an instruction could sit in the letters Sanborn chose freely (the K2 '?' marks, the extra letters of the panel rows); same word-shuffle controls do not apply there, so use row-order and letter-shuffle controls.

A word-level reading test: whole words picked by the K2 coordinates or by word counts (every k-th WORD read as a sentence), scored with a word-bigram model rather than letters; this run tests letters only.

Raise the detection limit for short messages by scoring only the acrostic family (6,600 word-letter readings instead of 44,876) with a pre-registered single statistic (longest common-word run); a 14-15 letter instruction would then stand out (controls' acrostic runs: median 10, max 18 here only because letter-skip readings are pooled in the combined test).
